paragraph: The work [began in March 2025 with Estonia's Digital Nation, funded by the World Bank](<https://lidermagazine.ao/governo-angolano-deu-inicio-dos-trabalhos-para-a-definicao-do-quadro-nacional-de-interoperabilidade/>). The Instituto de Modernização Administrativa's terms of reference of February 2026 say [a seven-month study with 25 public institutions produced a Framework and Roadmap of Interoperability](<https://sys.portais.gov.ao/uploads/Td_R_Consultoria_para_Implementacao_da_Interoperabilidade_da_Administracao_Publica_1_13f0252ef0.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a regional progress report says [the institute completed the framework study and its platform roadmap in the first half of 2026](<https://idea.comesa.int/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IDEA-Biannual-implementation-Progress-January-to-June-2026-V-J20-FK-006.pdf>). None of these sources names an instrument adopting the framework or gives a date for adoption. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

No stage is set. A May 2024 notice sought a consultant to write Burundi's government interoperability framework, and no later source says drafting began. Also found is the [EAC Secure Data Sharing Framework (proposed regional cross-border data flow framework)](<https://www.burunditimes.com/eac-backs-secure-data-sharing-framework-to-drive-regional-trade-innovation-and-growth/>), a regional proposal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No government interoperability framework has been found in drafting, adopted or required. Preparing would need a framework, standard or regulation for how government systems exchange data to be written or out for consultation.

The Cadre d'interopérabilité, published by the state digital agency, [is instituted by decree 2020-209 of 18 March 2020](<https://api.xroad.bj/documents/10/download>). It [sets four levels, juridical, organisational, semantic and technical, and five common infrastructure components](<https://api.xroad.bj/documents/10/download>). In May 2025 Benin told ID4Africa that [more than 120 systems had been integrated through](<https://www.id4africa.com/2025/files/T1-P2-S1-1_BENIN-final.pdf>) the exchange platform that runs under the framework. In the last twelve months, a new architecture policy for state information systems [went to sectoral consultation in Cotonou on 30 June 2026](<https://lanation.bj/actualites/transformation-numerique-de-letat-un-cadre-commun-pour-ses-systemes-dinformation-en-preparation>). The agency's legal note of July 2026 [treats the framework as in place](<https://asin.bj/doc/142/download>). [A national interoperability committee supervises](<https://asin.bj/doc/142/download>).

Burkina Faso's Référentiel général d'interopérabilité, [a normative document fixing the rules for compatibility between public administrations' information systems, was adopted by order of the Prime Minister on 23 May 2018](<https://burkina24.com/2019/10/15/burkina-un-referentiel-pour-moderniser-ladministration-publique/>). The account of the adoption [is a news report of 15 October 2019](<https://burkina24.com/2019/10/15/burkina-un-referentiel-pour-moderniser-ladministration-publique/>). It names no body charged with enforcing the rules. In the last twelve months the framework was cited and not changed. In May 2026 the government [told the World Health Assembly](<https://apps.who.int/gb/statements/WHA79/PDF/Burkina_Faso-12.6-12.10.pdf>) that its regulatory framework includes it. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

Section 12 of Botswana's Digital Services Act, assented to in October 2025, [requires the Digital Services Authority to establish a standardised Framework for Secure Exchange of Information](<http://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/digital_services_ACT.pdf>). The Act comes into force by ministerial order. A European Union-funded project running from August 2024 to August 2027 [is working with the government to improve and align the National Interoperability Framework](<https://www.expertisefrance.fr/en/projects/digital-transformation-botswana>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the exchange framework has been issued, and no public body is reported as bound by either text. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

Decree 2021-913 of 22 December 2021 [adopts the Référentiel Général d'Interopérabilité des Systèmes d'Information, annexed to it, as the general framework of technical rules for the interoperability of information systems](<https://anssi.gouv.ci/documents/28/décret_2021-913_du_22_décembre_2021_adoption_référentiel_général_dinteropérabilité_systèmes_dinformation.pdf>). Its third article binds public bodies to comply with the framework. The decree [was made on the joint report of the ministers for the digital economy and for the public service](<https://anssi.gouv.ci/documents/28/décret_2021-913_du_22_décembre_2021_adoption_référentiel_général_dinteropérabilité_systèmes_dinformation.pdf>), who are charged with carrying it out. It names no separate body that enforces compliance. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A workshop at Ebolowa from 3 to 14 November 2025 [gave technical validation to the draft e-government bill on access to public information and the digital transformation of the administration](<https://www.droitmediasfinance.com/index.php/actualites/droit-tech-fintech/1182-cameroun-la-legislation-sur-e-government-facilitant-lacces-a-linformation-publique-au-stade-de-la-validation-officielle>). The project that supports the reform says the bill [provides that administrations must make their information systems compatible, with GovTech Cameroun setting the security and interoperability norms](<https://patnuc.cm/2025/11/20/services-publics-et-transparence-les-evolutions-cles-de-la-loi-e-gov/>). No source found says the bill has been adopted. The account of 20 November 2025 gives no date for its passage through parliament. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The government [adopted the draft digital norms and standards for the public sector on 15 April 2022](<https://kt.cd/2022/04/16/adoption-du-projet-des-normes-et-standards-du-numerique-applicable-au-secteur-public/>), in five books that include the Référentiel Général d'Interopérabilité. A [workshop on 2-3 February 2022](<https://medd.gouv.cd/atelier-sur-lelaboration-et-adoption-des-referentiels-numeriques-du-secteur-public-en-rdc/>) had validated the books. The minister said the norms would be given legal force by ministerial order, and the article reports none as issued. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or order that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

Congo's digital economy ministry said on its news page of 2 September 2026 that the country [is committing to develop a National Digital Architecture built on the principles of digital public infrastructure](<https://numerique.gouv.cg/actualites/architecture-et-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi>). [The page describes it as the reference framework for interconnecting public and private information systems](<https://numerique.gouv.cg/actualites/architecture-et-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi>). The page dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. It cites no instrument adopting the architecture, gives no timetable and names no body that will hold it. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025 that its [Public Administration Information Systems Interoperability Framework is in draft or planned](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>). The survey line gives 2026 as the year. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, [IMIJ reported about 62 public and private institutions connected to its national identification systems](<https://justica.gov.cv/w/protocolo-de-interconex%C3%A3o-de-sistemas-dados-e-aplica%C3%A7%C3%B5es-entre-o-imij-i.p.-e-a-dire%C3%A7%C3%A3o-nacional-da-administra%C3%A7%C3%A3o-p%C3%BAblica-dnap->). NOSi runs [PDEX](<https://pdex.gov.cv/>), an API publication and subscription platform for the state. No source found says an interoperability framework is adopted and published. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The Agence Nationale des Systèmes d'Information de l'État [issued the Cadre d'Interopérabilité de Djibouti as the national interoperability framework](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/e3b093b92e0531dcb5994e53e1b0733d-0460012022/original/Cadre-d-Interop-rabilit-de-Djibouti.pdf>), setting out principles and four layers of interoperability. The document is dated 2022. [A consultancy says it drafted the national interoperability framework for the agency in a project that ran from May 2022 to April 2023](<https://ega.ee/project/djibouti-digital-interoperability-platform/>). Neither source names a decree or circular that makes the framework compulsory for ministries, and neither counts the public bodies that exchange data under it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

Executive decree 19-271 of 7 October 2019 [set a national interoperability framework for information systems](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2026/F2026017.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Journal officiel of 30 December 2025 carried presidential decree 25-320, which [makes the national interoperability system the exclusive framework for data exchange between public institutions and administrations](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2025/F2025087.pdf>). The decree puts the system under the High Commission for Digitalisation. On 20 September 2026 the Council of Ministers [ordered a further presidential decree on the secure digital interoperability plan between state bodies](<https://www.interfilalgerie.com/communique-du-conseil-des-ministres-45/>). No source names the bodies exchanging data under it. Mature would need a dated source that names or counts the public bodies that exchange data under the framework.

Egypt's [Cloud First Policy](<https://mcit.gov.eg/Upcont/Documents/Publications_2282024000_Cloud_First_Policy_Egypt_2024.pdf>), published in 2024, names the Supreme Council of Digital Society, its executive office and its specialised committees. It says they started developing national legislation on the classification, provision and exchange of official data and information. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology reported 105 government bodies connected to its [Government Digital Transformer](<https://www.almasdar.com/172314>). It also runs the [Government-to-Government project](<http://mcit.gov.eg/en/Media_Center/Press_Room/Press_Releases/98928>) with the Ministry of Interior. No adopted framework for how government systems exchange data has been found. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

No stage is set. No framework or draft has been found on record for Eritrea. No source dated in the last three years says the government has neither a framework nor one being written. Also found are [ASYCUDA World](<https://www.undp.org/eritrea/news/eritrea-launches-landmark-digital-customs-system-modernizing-trade>) and the [National identity card (new electronic card)](<https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2011310.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the government has no interoperability framework and none is being written.

The Ministry of Innovation and Technology's library of guidelines and standards [lists the Ethiopian Government Interoperability Framework of 2019 with the status Approved](<http://www.mint.gov.et/guidelines-standards/-/document_library/Ar4yXS04o1Ab/view/257247>). Its e-government assessment of February 2023 [refers to the approved framework](<http://www.mint.gov.et/documents/d/guest/final-mint-egov-services-evaluation-report-2023-?download=true>). It found that [the E-Services Portal offers no data interoperability features, a departure from the approved framework](<http://www.mint.gov.et/documents/d/guest/final-mint-egov-services-evaluation-report-2023-?download=true>). In July 2024 the ministry was [leading an interoperable digital government initiative, with a governance and compliance document for the framework attached](<https://www.capitalethiopia.com/2024/07/ethiopia-egovernment-interoperability>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A World Bank [appraisal document of 15 June 2021](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/301741627956043619/pdf/Gabon-Digital-Gabon-Project.pdf>) set a baseline of No for a common interoperability framework governing secure data exchange within government. In the last twelve months, as reported on 22 December 2025, the ANINF is [drawing up a national interoperability framework](<https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202512230269.html>) under the Gabon Digital programme. The report lists interoperability of public systems among the remaining challenges. No source found says the framework is adopted and published, or that a text requires public bodies to follow one. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The National Information Technology Agency's draft update says [the first Government of Ghana e-government interoperability framework, with the Government of Ghana Enterprise Architecture, was adopted in 2008](<https://nita.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Ghana-eGovernment-Interoperability-Framework-eGIF-Version-2.0_v.Draft-for-Stakeholder-Review-1.pdf>). [Version 2.0 of the framework is labelled a draft for stakeholder review](<https://nita.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Ghana-eGovernment-Interoperability-Framework-eGIF-Version-2.0_v.Draft-for-Stakeholder-Review-1.pdf>), dated 2022. The draft says [implementation of the 2008 framework was ineffectual and that the framework is out of date](<https://nita.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Ghana-eGovernment-Interoperability-Framework-eGIF-Version-2.0_v.Draft-for-Stakeholder-Review-1.pdf>). No source found says version 2.0 has been approved or names an instrument that makes either version compulsory. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

No stage is set. No framework or draft is on record for Guinea, and no source dated in the last three years says the government has neither. Also found are the document [Normes Procédures Règles d'Interopérabilité des SI v0.2.2](<https://ande.gov.gn/cadre-et-referentiels/>), [X-Road](<https://www.visionguinee.info/transformation-numerique-le-ministre-francois-bourouno-presente-a-bah-oury-deux-plateformes-pour-moderniser-ladministration-guineenne/>) and [GovStack](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/4820/guinea-launches-govstack-workshop-to-advance-digital-public-services>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a framework, standard or regulation for how government systems exchange data to be written or out for consultation.

In April 2026 the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy told a United Nations commission about [a national enterprise architecture framework, led by the government ICT agency](<https://unctad.org/system/files/non-official-document/ecn162026_s08_ai_gambia_en.pdf>). [It said the framework is ensuring interoperability across government systems through open standards, shared services and national governance](<https://unctad.org/system/files/non-official-document/ecn162026_s08_ai_gambia_en.pdf>). The statement dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. It gives no date of adoption and names no ministry exchanging data under it. It cites no decree, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The government [approved the regulation through Decree 27/2025, published in the Boletim Oficial of 31 October 2025](<https://wardip.gw/governo-aprova-regulamento-nacional-de-interoperabilidade-para-acelerar-a-transformacao-digital-na-guine-bissau/>). The Council of Ministers had [approved the draft decree on the Regulation on Interoperability of Systems and Digital Platforms of Public and Private Services in July 2025](<https://ang.gw/governo-aprova-projeto-de-regulamento-sobre-a-interoperabilidade-de-sistemas-e-plataformas-digitais/>). The regulation sets common technical standards so that systems can exchange data. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in August 2026 the programme [reported the national interoperability regulation as approved](<https://pt.linkedin.com/posts/wardip-guin%C3%A9-bissau_governo-aprova-regulamento-nacional-de-interoperabilidade-activity-7491768929355194368-Vk5Q>). The decree's text has not been found, and no source names the body that enforces it. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A World Bank diagnostic of 2024 [states that the government has no national interoperability framework and no government enterprise architecture framework](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). A report of July 2024 says [the diagnostic recommends a national interoperability framework, describing it as currently absent](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202407/world-bank-identifies-priority-actions-for-dpi-in-equatorial-guinea>). The diagnostic says [public sector systems do not communicate with each other](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated since 2024 reports a framework being drafted, and none names a body charged with writing one. Preparing would need a framework, standard or regulation for how government systems exchange data to be written or out for consultation.

The ICT Authority's published second edition of the Government Enterprise Architecture and Government Interoperability Framework [sets out an interoperability charter and data, technical and metadata standards](<https://cms.icta.go.ke/sites/default/files/2024-07/GEA%20-%20GIF%202nd%20Edition.pdf>). It leaves its approval date blank. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, [Kenya launched the ICT Authority Interoperability Framework, setting standards for government platforms to share data](<https://techweez.com/2026/04/29/kenya-ict-interoperability-framework-africa/>). Kenya's 2026/27 performance contract guidelines [make every ministry, county, department and agency put the architecture and framework in place](<https://digitalization.ict.go.ke/download.php?id=2>). Each [sends its architecture to the State Department for ICT for approval and registers its systems and APIs](<https://digitalization.ict.go.ke/download.php?id=2>). No source counts the bodies that have done so. Mature would need a dated source that names or counts the public bodies that exchange data under the framework.

No stage is set. No framework or draft is on record for Libya, and no source dated in the last three years says the government has neither. Also found are [LyGIF](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Libya-GIA-Interoperability-Plan2.pdf>) and the [National Directory of Government Data](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Libya-GIA-Interoperability-Plan2.pdf>), both in one linked document. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a framework, standard or regulation for how government systems exchange data to be written or out for consultation.

On 19 February 2025 the Minister of Finance and Development Planning told Parliament that [the Government of Lesotho Enterprise Architecture and Interoperability Framework is being developed](<https://www.rsl.org.ls/sites/default/files/2025-02/Budget%20Speech%202025%2026%20Final%2019-02-2025.pdf>). The government had [issued terms of reference for the Government of Lesotho Enterprise Architecture and a standalone e-Government Interoperability Framework](<https://www.gov.ls/download/terms-of-reference-for-development-of-the-government-of-lesotho-enterprise-archicture-glea-and-e-government-interoperability-e-gif-framework/>), on a page dated 22 July 2024. In the last twelve months the position was repeated and not changed. In March 2026 a consultancy said [it is supporting the Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation in developing the e-Government Interoperability Framework](<https://qualisysconsulting.com/en/blog/news-en-5/advancing-digital-government-in-lesotho-through-enterprise-architecture-and-interoperability-53>). No source found says the framework is adopted and published. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The World Bank's GovTech survey, in its 2025 round, [lists a General Interoperability Framework for Morocco as in draft or planned](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>), with 2026 as the framework's year. Morocco's Agency for Digital Development owns an [e-government interoperability platform built by Minsait](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/morocco-launches-e-government-interoperability-platform>), described in 2022. The same agency runs [Jisr](<https://www.lavieeco.com/au-royaume/plateforme-jisr-55-millions-doperations-dechange-de-donnees-enregistrees-en-une-annee/>), which recorded 55 million data exchange operations in one year, reported in February 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a government interoperability framework is adopted and published. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The digital governance unit [published version 1.0.2 of the Cadre d'interopérabilité, described as the first official interoperability framework in Madagascar](<https://digital.gov.mg/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/UGD-Cadre-dinterop%C3%A9rabilit%C3%A9V1.0.2.pdf>). It was validated on 10 November 2022 after drafts from December 2021. A decree followed: [decree 2025-1959 on the institutional framework of interoperability in Madagascar is listed on a legal portal, by title only](<https://observatoire-territoire.mg/lois/decret-n-2025-1959-relatif-au-cadre-institutionnel-de-linteroperabilite-a-madagascar/>). In the last twelve months, an article of April 2026 said [an exchange system is implemented within a legal framework reinforced by that decree](<https://newsmada.com/2026/04/29/systeme-rahaka-vers-linteroperabilite-nationale-des-donnees/>). The decree's text has not been found. What it requires of public bodies is not stated. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

[Decree 67/2017, approved by the Council of Ministers on 17 October 2017 and published on 1 December 2017, approves the Regulation of the e-Government Interoperability Framework](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_188_I_SERIE_2017.pdf>). It [applies to all public administration bodies, central and local](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_188_I_SERIE_2017.pdf>). It [obliges them to use a single interoperability platform and integrate their systems](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_188_I_SERIE_2017.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [a national workshop that opened on 11 June 2026 was the last consultation on the revised text before its final approval](<https://intic.gov.mz/decorre-a-fase-final-da-revisao-do-regulamento-do-quadro-de-interoperabilidade-de-sistemas-de-governo-digital-em-mocambique/>). On 23 October 2026 the national ICT institute [presented the proposed revision, which raises the guiding principles from 10 to 15](<https://pt.linkedin.com/posts/intic-instituto-nacional-de-tecnologias-de-informa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-e-comunica%C3%A7%C3%A3o_revis%C3%A3o-do-quadro-de-interoperabilidade-refor%C3%A7a-activity-7520792996766699521-sTTA>). Mature would need a dated source that names or counts the public bodies that exchange data under the framework.

A report of 27 March 2026 says the digital transformation ministry [held a three-day workshop to develop a unified framework of standards for public digital services, to ensure greater interoperability](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/03/27/mauritania-moves-to-standardize-public-digital-services-with-national-framework-initiative/>). [By September 2026 the ministry said a reference framework for the state's digital architecture standards had been drawn up](<https://trustmag.net/article/uODfIMtH>). [A Digital Architecture Council is planned to enforce it; the ministry did not say the framework was adopted](<https://trustmag.net/article/uODfIMtH>). All of this dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. The report names no decree, order or circular that would make the framework compulsory. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The government [issued version 1.0 of the Mauritius e-Government Interoperability Framework in November 2002, setting technical standards and specifications for interoperability across government information systems](<https://cib.govmu.org/Documents/Maintenance%20Agreement/egiframework.pdf>). The framework [covers data exchange between public agencies](<https://cib.govmu.org/Documents/Maintenance%20Agreement/egiframework.pdf>). Only one source has been found on it, and no later version is named. No source says it has been replaced or withdrawn. None names a decree, regulation or circular that makes it compulsory, or the public bodies that exchange data under it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A report of 11 June 2026 says the Ministry of ICT [has proposed a Government Data Sharing Regulation](<https://itweb.africa/article/malawi-devises-operational-rules-for-national-data-exchange-platform/xnklOvz1R2bq4Ymz>). [It would be a binding rule with a common digital standard so that government systems can communicate](<https://itweb.africa/article/malawi-devises-operational-rules-for-national-data-exchange-platform/xnklOvz1R2bq4Ymz>). It would [route all government data exchange through the National Data Centre](<https://itweb.africa/article/malawi-devises-operational-rules-for-national-data-exchange-platform/xnklOvz1R2bq4Ymz>). The proposal dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. The report gives no date for adoption, names no body that would enforce the rule and reports no ministry exchanging data under it. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The exchange platform's supplier says that [in 2014 it introduced an interoperability platform and a corresponding framework in Namibia](<https://cyber.ee/resources/case-studies/namibia/>). The Office of the Prime Minister [drafted an Interoperability Framework for Namibia, modelled on Estonia's X-Road, and consulted stakeholders on it in 2016](<https://mol.gov.na/documents/53329/0/EEC-+Expression+of+interest+Case+Management+System+01.10.2024+final.pdf/2c1d5f94-7353-c461-dc4d-95f00bc8125b>). The supplier adds that in a 2021-2022 project for the Office [it helped Namibia update its interoperability framework document](<https://cyber.ee/resources/case-studies/namibia/>). None of these accounts says the government adopted or published the framework, or names an instrument making it compulsory. No source found is dated after 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

A governors' forum report of July 2025 [rated Katsina State's alignment with the Nigeria e-Government Interoperability Framework as high](<https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/06/13/katsinas-digital-public-infrastructure-push-gaps-fixes-safeguards/>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the national IT agency [took over the Nigeria Government Enterprise Architecture framework from the Korean cooperation agency](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/03/27/nitda-takes-over-nigeria-government-enterprise-architecture-in-major-digital-governance-milestone/>). The work [took two and a half years](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/03/27/nitda-takes-over-nigeria-government-enterprise-architecture-in-major-digital-governance-milestone/>). The report describes the framework as [now operational and enabling data exchange across government agencies](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/03/27/nitda-takes-over-nigeria-government-enterprise-architecture-in-major-digital-governance-milestone/>). It cites no instrument that makes the framework compulsory, and no source found says the agency enforces it. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A news report says [Rwanda approved its National Data Sharing Policy in May 2025, to provide a framework for data exchange between public institutions](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/39395/news/health/africa-needs-to-take-charge-of-its-digital-health-systems-says-minister>). Before the policy, a 2019 survey of eight public agencies [found no common standards, guidelines, interoperability framework or enterprise architecture, and recommended publishing one](<https://dr.ur.ac.rw/handle/123456789/1229>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated since the policy's approval names an instrument that makes it compulsory or a body that enforces it. The policy's text has not been found. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

[On 26 March 2026 a steering committee validated a national interoperability framework and a draft decree](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/mctnsn_newdealtechnologique-interop%C3%A9rabilit%C3%A9-activity-7443068023738900480-ejtp>), the first phase's output. [On 28 and 29 April 2026 it met the health ministry to build the framework's health version](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/mctnsn_newdealtechnologique-activity-7461126186086227968-NqZh>). [On 5 May 2026 the digital ministry was to present the draft decree](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/mctnsn_dpi-newdealtechnologique-activity-7457180609757528065-UqRT>). All of this dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. No source found says the decree or the framework has been adopted. In August the ministry [said the inventory of state systems was still to be drawn up](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202608/senegal-seeks-to-fully-align-sovereignty-vision-with-dpi-strategy>). Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation said in October 2025 that [a Government Enterprise Architecture Framework it developed will serve as a national guide for digital integration](<https://mocti.gov.sl/mocti-trains-over-100-ict-professionals-to-strengthen-digital-skills-to-design-develop-and-maintain-robust-enterprise-architecture/>). It also [trained over 100 ICT officers from ministries, departments and agencies in enterprise architecture](<https://mocti.gov.sl/mocti-trains-over-100-ict-professionals-to-strengthen-digital-skills-to-design-develop-and-maintain-robust-enterprise-architecture/>). Its statement does not say the framework has been adopted or published. It cites no instrument that would make it compulsory, and names no body that would enforce it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

In August 2025 the Ministry of Communications and Technology's e-Government Strategy 2025-2029 [said the federal government had no enterprise architecture or interoperability framework](<https://moct.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/eGovernment-Strategy-2025-2029.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 27 October 2026, the Office of the Prime Minister and the ministry [held a national workshop to validate the National Digital Coordination Framework](<https://hiiraanweyn.net/dowladda-soomaaliya-oo-ansixinaysa-qaab-dhismeedka-qaranka-ee-isku-duwidda-dowladda-dijitaalka-ah/>). It covers the coordination, interoperability and alignment of federal government digital systems. No adopted text of the framework has been found, and no body has been found charged with enforcing one. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

The regulations list of the national innovation institute, INIC, [names Lei 1/2024 Quadro Nacional de Interoperabilidade](<https://inic.gov.st/regulamentacao.php>), though the text of the 2024 law is not posted. The national cybersecurity strategy has a final version dated 15 December 2023. It records that [the Quadro Nacional de Interoperabilidade was published in November 2021](<https://www.ager.st/images/estrategia_cyber_.pdf>). It also says that [a Lei de Interoperabilidade was at the time a draft bill](<https://www.ager.st/images/estrategia_cyber_.pdf>). In the last twelve months the law was cited and not changed. In October 2026 the justice minister [cited the 2024 framework law among the country's legislative initiatives](<https://rafa.tl/pt/sao-tome-e-principe-defende-mecanismos-mais-rapidos-para-obter-provas-digitais-entre-paises-da-cplp/>). No source found names a body that enforces the framework. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

The Office of the Executive Secretary, e-Governance, in the Ministry of ICT [published the Eswatini e-Government Interoperability Framework v1.0](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RAMquPzUfBt2Jz0EJn7oB2viNFr17vE8/view?usp=drive_link>) in March 2025. It sets technical policies and standards for how government systems interconnect and exchange data. An [IOM assessment from a mission in October 2022](<https://publications.iom.int/system/files/pdf/pub2023-114-r-iom-mmdma-report-eswatini.pdf>) had described a government interoperability framework as a submitted proposal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a decree, law, regulation or circular makes the framework compulsory, or names the body that enforces it. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

No stage is set. No framework or draft is on record for Chad, and no source dated in the last three years says the government has neither. Also found are the [Integrated public finance management system (SIGFiP)](<https://lendjampost.com/budget-2027-le-tchad-mise-sur-le-numerique-pour-verrouiller-les-finances-publiques/>), the [National biometric registry](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202603/chad-uses-national-biometric-registry-to-boost-govt-systems-interoperability>) and the [e-Visa](<https://lendjampost.com/budget-2027-le-tchad-mise-sur-le-numerique-pour-verrouiller-les-finances-publiques/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the government has no interoperability framework and none is being written.

The Agence Togo Digital sets out the government's Cadre Commun d'Interopérabilité in its Guide de l'Architecture d'Entreprise. [The guide's version-control page shows version 1.0 with the status Brouillon](<https://ressources.digital.gouv.tg/shares/documentations/Guide_architecture_national/html/controle_version.html>), meaning draft. [It shows a blank version date and an empty revision history](<https://ressources.digital.gouv.tg/shares/documentations/Guide_architecture_national/html/controle_version.html>). The page [was captured on 6 September 2026 and carries no date of its own](<https://ressources.digital.gouv.tg/shares/documentations/Guide_architecture_national/html/controle_version.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. It names no decree, order or circular adopting the guide or making it compulsory, and no body that would enforce it. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.

[Decree-law 2020-31 of the Head of Government, published in the Official Journal of 10 June 2020, concerns electronic data exchange between public bodies and their users and between the bodies themselves](<https://www.marchespublics.gov.tn/fr/legislations/5923/download>). [Government decree 2020-777 of 5 October 2020 sets the conditions and procedures for that exchange, implementing the decree-law](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-gouvernemental-n-2020-777-du-5-octobre-2020-fixant-les-conditions-les-modalites-et-les-procedures-dapplication-du-decret-loi-du-chef-du-gouvernement-n-2020-31-du-10-juin/>). The decree [defines a national interoperability operator and an interoperability system](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-gouvernemental-n-2020-777-du-5-octobre-2020-fixant-les-conditions-les-modalites-et-les-procedures-dapplication-du-decret-loi-du-chef-du-gouvernement-n-2020-31-du-10-juin/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The passages found show titles and definitions and not the provisions that follow. No source says public bodies must use the system or that the operator enforces the rules. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

The e-Government Agency [issued the e-Government Interoperability Framework, version 1.0, approved by its chief executive in February 2016](<https://www.ega.go.tz/uploads/standards/sw-1574945623-inter.pdf>). The framework [sets common standards and technical guidelines for public institutions to exchange data](<https://www.ega.go.tz/uploads/standards/sw-1574945623-inter.pdf>). It is the agency's own document, and the only source found that states the rule. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory for public institutions, or says the agency enforces it or counts the institutions that comply. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

[The published Uganda e-Government Interoperability Framework was issued by the ICT ministry and the national IT authority and dated 6 May 2021](<https://www.nita.go.ug/sites/default/files/2025-07/e-GIF.pdf>). It sets twelve principles and six interoperability layers for e-government systems. In the last twelve months, the framework's renewal [was launched with a multi-agency workshop in Kampala in February 2026](<https://ega.ee/uganda-renewal-government-enterprise-architecture-interoperability-framework/>). By May 2026 [the government had renewed the Government Enterprise Architecture and the framework, with World Bank support](<https://ega.ee/uganda-renewed-digital-government-frameworks/>). No source names an instrument that makes the framework compulsory, counts the bodies following it, or names the body that enforces the renewed framework. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

[In a reply to a question of 28 August 2025](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/32258/>), the Department of Public Service and Administration told Parliament it had published the Minimum Interoperability Standards. It presents them as guidance for departments. In the last twelve months, [Operation Vulindlela's report for April to June 2026](<https://www.treasury.gov.za/comm_media/press/2026/Operation%20Vulindlela%20Progress%20Report%20Q1%20-%202026.pdf>) says work progressed on updating them. The update was to be tested in priority digital services by September 2026. No instrument has been found that makes the standards compulsory or names who enforces them, and no department is reported following them. Operating would need public bodies to be required to follow the framework.

The government, through the electronic government division in the Office of the President, [issued the Public Service ICT Electronic Government Interoperability Standard, first edition, in a final version dated February 2019](<https://policyvault.africa/wp-content/uploads/policy/ZMB588.pdf>). The text describes itself as the electronic government interoperability framework for all ministries, provinces and spending agencies. The standard [is a government-issued document and cites no decree or law behind it](<https://policyvault.africa/wp-content/uploads/policy/ZMB588.pdf>). It says of itself that the division enforces it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated since 2019 names a law that makes it compulsory or counts the bodies checked against it. Operating would need a decree, law, regulation or circular that makes the framework compulsory and names the body that enforces it.

A supplier says it [completed an enterprise architecture framework, roadmap and change plan for the government](<https://ega.ee/project/enterprise-architecture-zimbabwe/>), in a project that ran from September 2023 to September 2024. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, [the Enterprise Architecture Model blueprint was officially handed over](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/5347/zimbabwe-pushes-smart-government-agenda-with-new-digital-blueprint>). The ICT minister said [the blueprint was handed to the nation's ICT directors](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hon-tatenda-mavetera-7821b96b_digitalizezimbabwe-vision2030-zimbabweisopenfordigitalbusiness-activity-7458359047386234880-OgCR>) at a conference of 7 May 2026. A Herald column of November 2026 says the government is [building a whole-of-government enterprise architecture that defines interoperability standards](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/transforming-public-services-through-one-digital-ecosystem/>). No source names an instrument making the blueprint compulsory or says it has been published. Establishing would need a framework for how government systems exchange data to be adopted and published.
